explanation: Tipping is not mandatory in Saudi Arabia and service-sector wages aren't structured around gratuities, but leaving roughly 10-15% in cash is increasingly common and appreciated, especially where no service charge is listed. Reporting on local attitudes notes views are genuinely mixed — some Saudis see it as generous hospitality, others as closer to alms for foreign workers, and Saudis rarely tip fellow Saudis.
local_tip: Check the bill for a service charge first; if there isn't one, leaving 10-15% in cash is a safe, appreciated amount.

also_check.note: Tipping is not local custom and can confuse staff, since excellent service is already expected without extra payment.
Tipping 15-20% is standard and forms a real part of server income.
Service is included by law, but leaving a little extra for exceptional service is a polite touch.

sources.title: Tips for women travelling to Saudi
